_comment: Phase 32 §32.5 step 6 — 20-claim hand-labeled probe set for the /ground/claim retrieval layer. expected ∈ {EVIDENCE, SILENT}: v1 grounds at the RETRIEVAL level, so a contradiction-of-a-known-result expects EVIDENCE (the contradicted literature must surface for the professor/panel contracrow step to catch it); genuinely-open claims expect SILENT (corpus absence = the novelty signal). Bar: ≥80% verdict accuracy, zero fabricated citation keys (every returned key must exist in the corpus).

the average of big Omega(n) minus omega(n) converges to the sum over primes of 1/(p(p-1)), approximately 0.7731
the natural density of squarefree integers equals 6 over pi squared
the natural density of abundant numbers is approximately 0.2476
the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture gives the twin prime counting function with the twin prime constant 2 C2 approximately 1.32
the error term in the Dirichlet divisor problem has exponent between 1/4 and 131/416
Cramer's conjecture states that maximal gaps between consecutive primes are of order log squared p
the Erdos-Kac theorem says omega(n) is asymptotically normally distributed with mean and variance log log n
under the Riemann Hypothesis the Mertens function M(x) is bounded by x to the power 1/2 plus epsilon
the normal order of the number of distinct prime factors omega(n) is log log n by Hardy and Ramanujan
the natural density of abundant numbers is approximately 0.45
the average order of the divisor function d(n) grows linearly in n
maximal gaps between consecutive primes grow exponentially in log p

the Mertens function M(x) exceeds x to the power 0.9 infinitely often

the maximal prime gap below x is bounded by 0.506 times log squared x with relative slack 0.002 near x = 200000
